claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

1. **Do you have any children you're responsible for?** If yes, how many children, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 18 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to ask some questions about Alex to determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

Since Alex is 18 years old, the key factor is whether he's in approved education or training. Child Benefit can continue for children under 20 if they're in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he studying at school, college, sixth form, or doing an approved training course?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's studying for his A-levels at college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Since Alex is 18 and studying for his A-levels at college, he would generally qualify as being in approved education.

Now I need to ask about your own circumstances:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your responsibility for Alex:

**Does Alex live with you, or if he lives elsewhere (for example at college accommodation), do you contribute at least the equivalent of Child Benefit towards his upkeep** (such as for food, clothes, or pocket money)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Now I need to check a few more things:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, another parent or guardian?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Has Alex started any paid work for 24 hours or more per week, or is he claiming any benefits in his own right** (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He does receive Universal Credit in his own name, actually.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that important information. That's a crucial detail for your eligibility.

Just to confirm my understanding: **Alex is receiving Universal Credit in his own name while he's studying his A-levels at college - is that correct?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct. He receives Universal Credit in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Unfortunately, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

While you meet most of the standard requirements - you live in the UK, Alex lives with you, he's in approved education (studying A-levels), and nobody else is claiming for him - there is an important rule that affects your eligibility:

**Child Benefit stops when a child starts receiving certain benefits in their own right, including Universal Credit.** Since Alex is receiving Universal Credit in his own name, this means you cannot claim Child Benefit for him, even though he's still under 20 and in approved education.

I'm sorry this isn't the outcome you were hoping for. If Alex's circumstances change in the future (for example, if he stops claiming Universal Credit), your eligibility situation may be different at that time.
